clue.text: Fine weather that came from Berlin

definitions.note: a description of a song rather than a synonym

blocks.note: first meaning: a cloudless sky on a sunny day
second meaning: a 1926 song written by Irving Berlin

explanation.surface: A meteorologist remarks that a spell of sunshine drifted over from the German capital.
explanation.walkthrough: Berlin looks like the German city, but it is the songwriter Irving Berlin, who wrote the standard Blue Skies.
explanation.definitionFit: Clear cloudless heavens are the classic picture of good weather, and the phrase is also the title of Irving Berlin's song.

clue.text: Pulses that sound like roots

indicators.note: the clue tells us the answer is pronounced the same as a word for the roots

blocks.note: beetroots are root vegetables; the answer is spelt differently but said the same

explanation.surface: Something rhythmic is said to resemble the underground parts of plants.
explanation.definitionFit: Regular throbs of the heart, or rhythmic strokes in music, are both called beats as well as pulses.

clue.text: Ignorant, or deliberately forgotten?

blocks.note: first meaning: lacking education
second meaning: read as ..., i.e. a habit or fact purposely discarded

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a person simply never knew, or chose to put the knowledge out of mind.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful second reading, taking the word apart as the reverse of having learned something.
explanation.definitionFit: An uneducated person is unlearned (an adjective), while a lesson consciously dropped has been unlearned (a past participle).

clue.text: Deferential communication from Captain Nemo?

blocks.note: Nemo commands the submarine Nautilus in Jules Verne's novel; sub is short for submarine
a missive is a letter or message

explanation.surface: A meek letter arrives from the fictional commander of the Nautilus.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the clue as a letter from a submarine: a sub's missive. The question mark admits the playful split.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone deferential yields readily to others' wishes, which is the core meaning of being obedient or meek.

clue.text: Popular soft drink for princess

blocks.note: in fashion, i.e. popular
a brand of fizzy orange drink

explanation.surface: A trendy fizzy beverage is offered to a royal daughter.
explanation.definitionFit: An infanta is a daughter of a Spanish or Portuguese monarch, a royal title equivalent to princess.

clue.text: Went off to capture carbon: thoroughly cleaned!

indicators.note: capturing something means holding it inside, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: milk that has gone off has turned sour
C is the chemical symbol for carbon

explanation.surface: Something spoiled and soaked up soot, yet came out spotless.
explanation.definitionFit: To scour is to scrub hard with something abrasive, so a scoured pot has been cleaned vigorously.

clue.text: Hoist weight a tiny distance

blocks.note: W is the abbreviation for weight
an inch is a very short length

explanation.surface: A crane lifts a load just fractionally off the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: A winch is a lifting machine with a drum and cable, so it is a kind of hoist.

clue.text: Come to late party

blocks.note: first meaning: regain consciousness, stir from sleep
second meaning: a gathering held for someone who has died, the late person

explanation.surface: An invitation to drop by a party that starts after hours.
explanation.walkthrough: Late suggests a party at night, but it means deceased: the gathering mourns the dead.
explanation.definitionFit: To wake is to come round from sleep, and a wake is a vigil or gathering after a funeral.

clue.text: Is 4 minus 3 two? Not a person answers

blocks.note: the reply to the question is a denial
the arithmetic gives the correct result

explanation.surface: A simple arithmetic quiz, with the answer supplied by nobody at all.
explanation.walkthrough: Reply to the sum: no, it is one. Run together, the two words of that reply give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Nobody, nobody at all: the phrase means not a single person.

clue.text: You once put in pipes for orangeries, for example

indicators.note: putting something in places it inside another thing

blocks.note: the archaic form of you
hoses are flexible pipes

explanation.surface: A plumber is told to fit pipework in the glasshouses where citrus grows.
explanation.walkthrough: The archaic word goes inside the pipes, after their first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An orangery is a heated glass building for growing tender plants, one example of a greenhouse kept warm.

clue.text: I’m not prepared to come out with this

definitions.text: I’m not prepared to come out with this

blocks.clueFragment: I’m not prepared to come out with this
blocks.note: surface reading: someone refusing to reveal or admit something
setter's reading: unrehearsed, so what one comes out with is improvised on the spot

explanation.surface: Someone declines to make a statement or confession.
explanation.walkthrough: Not prepared reads as unwilling, but means unrehearsed: a remark made up as you go along.
explanation.definitionFit: An improvised remark or performance is said off the cuff, made without any rehearsal or script.

clue.text: Fact: crook sports a very formal garment

indicators.note: a sport in biology is a mutation, so these letters mutate into a new order

blocks.note: the two words supply the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: It is a fact: the villain is wearing smart formal dress.
explanation.walkthrough: Sports looks like wears, as of clothing; here it signals mutation.
explanation.definitionFit: A frock coat is a knee-length double-breasted Victorian man's coat, now worn only on very formal occasions.

clue.text: At halt, a railway is stuck?

blocks.note: a halt is a small railway stopping place, a minor station
taken as written
RY is the abbreviation for railway

explanation.surface: A train halted at a minor station asks whether the line is jammed.
explanation.definitionFit: Something stationary is not moving at all, motionless, which is how a stuck object behaves.

clue.text: Power to reject spoiled vote

indicators.note: something spoiled is ruined, so its letters are damaged into another order

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A spoiled ballot paper gives someone the power to block a result.
explanation.definitionFit: A veto is the right to block a decision or law, the authority to refuse assent.

clue.text: One predicts you a starry future

definitions.text: One predicts you a starry future

blocks.clueFragment: One predicts you a starry future
blocks.note: surface reading: someone forecasting that you will become a celebrity
setter's reading: a future read from the stars and planets in a horoscope

explanation.surface: A talent scout tells you that fame awaits.
explanation.walkthrough: Starry suggests stardom; it means the stars of the zodiac, whose positions this person claims to read.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who casts horoscopes foretells events from the positions of celestial bodies.

clue.text: In card game, is Daisy able to speak perhaps?

indicators.note: the words are to be spoken out, so what matters is the sound, not the spelling

blocks.note: to be able is to can
the daisy belongs to the aster family; said in a non-rhotic accent it ends in -ta

explanation.surface: During a card game, someone wonders whether a woman called Daisy can talk.
explanation.walkthrough: Daisy looks like a woman's name but is the flower. Ask can aster? aloud and the card game is heard.
explanation.definitionFit: Canasta is a rummy-style card game played with two packs, popular from the mid-twentieth century.

clue.text: Pest chewed rock in bus

indicators.note: something chewed is broken up and mashed, so its letters are jumbled
one thing being in another means it sits inside it

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange
a coach is a long-distance bus

explanation.surface: A pest gnawed through a stone lodged inside a bus.
explanation.definitionFit: The cockroach is a scavenging insect that infests kitchens, a classic household pest.

clue.text: Allow to go and be rude to teacher

blocks.note: dis is slang for disrespect or insult
pupils address a female teacher as Miss

explanation.surface: A pupil asks to leave early and then insults the teacher.
explanation.definitionFit: To dismiss someone is to let them leave, as a class is sent away at the end of a lesson.

clue.text: Smooth illiterate’s “signature” for military decoration

blocks.note: to iron is to press smooth
someone unable to write signs with an X mark

explanation.surface: A soldier who cannot write makes a neat mark to receive a medal.
explanation.definitionFit: The Iron Cross is a Prussian and German medal awarded for bravery in battle.

clue.text: Body of potholer a daughter buried

indicators.note: something buried lies inside something else, so these letters go within

blocks.note: a potholer explores caves
taken as written
D is the abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: The remains of a cave explorer, with his daughter interred too.
explanation.walkthrough: A potholer is a British term for a caver, someone who explores underground caves.
explanation.definitionFit: A cadaver is a dead human body, especially one used for dissection, so it means a corpse.

clue.text: Exposed position of troop destroyed

indicators.note: something destroyed is wrecked, so its letters fall into a different order

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A unit of soldiers is wiped out in a vulnerable spot.
explanation.definitionFit: The top of a roof is high and unsheltered, a place open to the weather and to view.

clue.text: Inquisitive scoundrel is casing university

indicators.note: a casing surrounds what it holds, so the next part goes inside

blocks.note: a cur is a contemptible man
taken as written
OU is the Open University

explanation.surface: A nosy rogue is staking out a college to rob it.
explanation.walkthrough: Casing suggests a burglar's reconnaissance, but here it means enclosing. The Open University is Britain's distance-learning university.
explanation.definitionFit: Being curious means eager to know or learn things, which is to be inquisitive.

clue.text: Formal new instructions here for leaving

definitions.text: Formal new instructions here for leaving

blocks.clueFragment: Formal new instructions here for leaving
blocks.note: surface reading: an official notice about how to depart, such as an exit procedure
setter's reading: leaving as bequeathing property in a will

explanation.surface: An official notice gives updated directions for departing the building.
explanation.walkthrough: Leaving suggests going away, but means leaving things to heirs: the document adds new terms to a will.
explanation.definitionFit: A codicil is a supplement to a will, formally amending or adding to its bequests.

clue.text: Wax and massage at end of play

definitions.note: the answer is the first name that goes with Wax

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, so only that one is kept

blocks.note: to massage is to rub
the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A beauty salon offers waxing and a massage after the show.
explanation.walkthrough: Wax looks like a beauty treatment, but it is the surname of Ruby Wax, the American-born comedian and TV presenter famous in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruby Wax is a comedian, so the first name pairs with the surname given in the clue.

clue.text: A stick and a bit of carrot?

blocks.note: first meaning: a conductor's or relay runner's rod
second meaning: a vegetable cut into a thin oblong strip

explanation.walkthrough: Stick and carrot together suggest the reward-and-punishment saying, but each is a separate meaning of the same word.
explanation.definitionFit: A baton is a short rod, and in cookery a baton is a thin stick-shaped strip of cut vegetable.

clue.text: Hungry and sleepy girl who found her comfort zone?

definitions.text: Hungry and sleepy girl who found her comfort zone?

blocks.note: surface reading: any tired, peckish young woman
setter's reading: the fairy-tale girl who sampled porridge and beds until one was just right

explanation.surface: A tired, hungry young woman finally finds somewhere she feels at ease.
explanation.walkthrough: The heroine of the bears' fairy tale ate porridge and slept in beds until finding ones neither too hot nor too cold; a just-right zone is now named after her.
explanation.definitionFit: The fairy-tale girl tried the three bears' porridge and beds; her name is used for anything at an ideal middle level.

clue.text: In place, observed to speak

indicators.note: speaking means saying the word out, so the sound counts and not the spelling

blocks.note: observed means seen, spotted

explanation.surface: Someone in position has been noticed and is invited to talk.
explanation.definitionFit: Something sited has been located or positioned, put in its place.

clue.text: Old city Des goes on to devastate

indicators.note: when something goes it departs, so those letters are removed

blocks.note: to devastate is to wreck
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man named Des moves on to lay waste to an ancient city.
explanation.walkthrough: Des looks like a man's name, but it is just the first three letters of the verb to be removed.
explanation.definitionFit: Troy is the ancient city besieged by the Greeks in Homer's Iliad, in modern Turkey.

clue.text: Circle Line train cat disturbed, finally caught

definitions.note: the answer is the word that names this line of latitude, the ___ Circle

indicators.note: things disturbed are thrown into disorder, so the letters are muddled

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange
C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught, and finally places it last

explanation.surface: On the London Underground's Circle Line, a cat upsets a train before being captured.
explanation.walkthrough: Circle Line looks like the London Tube route; it is a line of latitude round the South Pole.
explanation.definitionFit: The Antarctic Circle is the line of latitude near 66 degrees south, ringing the southern polar region.

clue.text: Good landlord offers spirit

blocks.note: G is the abbreviation for good
a pub landlord is mine host

explanation.surface: A kindly pub landlord serves up some strong liquor.
explanation.walkthrough: Spirit looks like a drink from the bar; it is a phantom.
explanation.definitionFit: A ghost is the spirit of a dead person said to appear to the living.

clue.text: Funny rhyme for a term of endearment

blocks.note: a word that rhymes with funny

explanation.surface: A comic poem written as a pet name for a loved one.
explanation.walkthrough: Funny looks like an adjective describing the rhyme; it is the word to be rhymed with.
explanation.definitionFit: Honey is an affectionate way to address a partner, like darling or sweetheart.

clue.text: The Northern Star edition sharply divided opinion

blocks.note: Polaris is the Pole Star, above the North Pole
ED is the abbreviation for edition

explanation.surface: An issue of a newspaper called The Northern Star proved controversial with readers.
explanation.walkthrough: The Northern Star looks like a newspaper title, the sense edition supports, but it is the star itself.
explanation.definitionFit: To polarise is to split people into two opposing camps, so a polarising issue divides views sharply.
